title: MACHINE SHED BLAZE
full_story:
On Tuesday, at approximately 7:55 pm, the Xenia Fire Protection District was dispatched to the 1500 block of Lion Lane for a reported machine shed fire.

Upon arrival, command staff located a 40-by-60-foot machine shed with flames visible from the rear wall and roof area of the structure.  Due to the size and intensity of the fire, mutual aid was requested from the North Clay Fire Protection District.

Firefighters faced several challenges during the incident, including limited access to the structure, multiple pieces of equipment inside the shed, and multiple explosions during the early stages of firefighting operations.

Despite firefighters’ efforts, the machine shed was deemed a complete loss, along with its contents.  Equipment destroyed in the fire included a combine, tractor, planter, seed drill, grain truck, and other miscellaneous items.  A grain cart parked outside in close proximity to the structure was also lost.

The Xenia Fire Protection District responded with two engines, a tanker, a brush truck, and 14 members.  The North Clay Fire Protection District provided mutual aid with 26 members, a tanker, an equipment truck, and a squad.

Firefighters remained on scene for approximately two and a half hours battling the blaze and working to extinguish the fire.

The cause of the fire is believed to have originated with one of the pieces of equipment parked inside the machine shed.

The Xenia Fire Protection District thanks the North Clay Fire Protection District for its assistance and support during this incident.

title: TRICK OR TREAT NIGHTS
full_story:
In Flora and Clay City Trick or Treat night will be tonight from 6 to 8 pm.  The Flora Church of the Nazarene will also have Treats N’ Eats tonight, from 6 to 8 pm. They will be serving hot dogs, chips, popcorn, hot chocolate, coffee and water, plus lots of candy for the kids.  Everyone is welcome.

Noble will have Halloween activities on Friday at the Noble Park, Trick-or-Treat hours for the village will be Saturday from 6 to 8 pm.

The Village of Cisne will host its annual Trunk or Treat and Fall Festival tomorrow night, in the Cisne Square.  Activities begin at 4:30 pm with trunk or treat, cake walk, costume judging, parade, and bingo.  The parade will feature the Cisne High School and Middle School bands.  Participants are encouraged to decorate their side-by-sides, golf carts, or four-wheelers for the parade lineup on the east side of Key Market.

The Cisne Fire Department will also hold a fundraiser supper Friday evening, beginning at 4 pm at the firehouse.  The menu is chili, peanut-butter sandwiches, desserts, and drinks.  Dine-in and carry-out options will be available.  Cost is by donation and all proceeds will benefit Christmas for Kids in the North Wayne School District.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade is Saturday night, at 7:00 pm.  There is no theme, so entrants can use their own creativity when planning the entry.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Please register at the chamber no later than Noon tomorrow.  The Chamber office is open tomorrow from 8 am to 5 pm.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15 pm.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after Noon tomorrow.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

title: SANTA SMILES APPLICATIONS
full_story:
Applications for Santa Smiles need to be turned in by Sunday.

Applications can be picked up at the Clay City Village Hall, Xenia Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, Louisville Banking Company, or Salt & Strings Butchery.  In Flora applications are available at the Flora City Hall, Flora Library, CEFS, and the office of Todd Fender at the Clay County Housing Authority.  The Clay County Health Department will give their applications to their clients.

Applications can be dropped off at the Clay City Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, and Xenia City Hall.  In Flora Applications can be dropped off at the Clay County Housing authority night drop box.  Applications can also be mailed.

Last year Santa Smiles provided gifts to 523 kids, and 71 residents at Chestnut Corner Sheltered Care in Louisville.

title: YOUTH HUNT
full_story:
Dan Hecht is having a free Youth Bird Hunt on Saturday November 7th.  The hunt is for those ages 10 – 16 wanting to experience Quail and Pheasant Hunting.  The location is the Hecht farm at 3362 Riffle Road near Iola, about 20 minutes South of Effingham.  The hunt times are from 9 am to 4 pm.

There will be Clay Pigeons for warm up, practice, and instruction.  There will be fields for first timers, as well as fields for the experienced hunters.

There will be a raffle to win a gun.  To help conservation efforts there will also be memberships for Quail Forever available.

Hunters should be sure to get a regular hunting License or an apprentice hunting license.  A gun safety course would be beneficial for Safety.

Please call the dealership and tell the receptionist that you want to attend the Youth Hunt in the morning or afternoon and how many will be attending.  The Phone number is 217-342-4111 or 217-821-4112 or email [email protected].

title: SEX OFFENDER COMPLIANCE CHECKS
full_story:
The Wayne County Sheriff’s Office, in coordination with the Fairfield Police Department, has completed annual compliance checks on all registered sex offenders in Wayne County ahead of Halloween trick or treating hours.

During these checks, the Wayne County Sheriff’s Office made multiple arrests involving individuals who failed to properly register, including one individual registered out of Carroll County, Illinois for failure to register.

The safety of our communities’ children is our highest priority.  We remain committed to holding offenders accountable and working together to ensure our communities are as safe as possible for our families.

The Wayne County Sheriff’s office thanks the Fairfield Police Department for its partnership and continued commitment to keeping our communities safe.

title: HUNTERS FEEDING ILLINOIS
full_story:
A popular program returns for its fifth season to help feed neighbors in need.  Hunters Feeding Illinois connects hunters, meat processors, and food pantries to bring lean protein to local residents and families, providing a unique pathway to address and improve food insecurity.

In partnership with Feeding Illinois, Access Illinois Outdoors, Southern Illinois Food Pantry Network, and University of Illinois Extension, the program allows hunters to donate harvested deer to partnering meat processors who turn it into ground meat.  Food pantries receive ground venison to share with their guests.

“Food insecurity affects about one in eight Illinois residents, and the challenge is even greater across much of our program area,” said Michelle Fombelle, food and health systems educator.  “With the rising cost of protein, Hunters Feeding Illinois helps ensure families can put nutritious meals on the table while making their food dollars go further.”

Like previous years, hunters can donate whole harvested deer at no cost.  Because processing volume increases throughout the season, hunters are encouraged to call processors in advance to confirm they have slots to accept deer.  Processors have a select number of slots for donated deer, which become more limited as the season continues.

Partnering processors in our area for the hunting season include Blair’s Slaughtering and Processing, and Salt and Strings butchery both in Louisville.

Thanks to our collaboration with Feeding Illinois, donations are doubled dollar for dollar.  A $50 donation becomes $100, which covers the processing of one deer.  Donate online at go.illinois.edu/deerdonation.

During the 2025-2026 hunting season, Hunters Feeding Illinois distributed 40,712 pounds of ground venison to 43 food pantries across east-central and southern Illinois.

To learn more, connect on Facebook, join the email list, or email [email protected].  Visit the website at go.illinois.edu/deerdonation for recipes, videos, and more program information.

title: IDOT CAREER FAIR
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation is hosting a career fair in Effingham on Thursday, November 5th.  The career fair will be held from 10 am to 2 pm at the Effingham County Emergency Management Agency, 311 West Miracle Avenue, in Effingham.

Staff will be on site to discuss technical and administrative support opportunities for multiple IDOT job locations throughout the area.

“This event is an excellent opportunity for the public to learn about the employment options available at IDOT,” said Illinois Department of Transportation Region Four Engineer Teresa Price.  “As an engineer who has worked in both the public and private sectors, I can attest to the exemplary work environment at IDOT that not only offers strong employment opportunities but also helps mentor and train employees for long-term careers.”

Attendees will learn how to apply for state jobs.  Central Management Services will be on hand to explain the application process and offer in-person guidance for creating a state employment profile, applying for state positions and other best practices for pursuing a career with the state of Illinois. Attendees are encouraged to bring their own laptop.

The Illinois Secretary of State’s office will have staff present to answer questions on obtaining a commercial driver’s license for positions where one is required.

The event is free and open to the public.  Registration is recommended but not required.  To register, visit IDOT Career Fair or contact IDOT’s Office of Diversity and Recruitment at [email protected].

To find out more about working at IDOT, including current job openings, pay and benefits, visit IDOT Employment Opportunities.
